title: Boasting of every theatre played; the show Hot Chops and songs he wrote
summary: He lists theatres from Los Angeles to Glasgow, mentions the act's own show Hot Chops and a song about Buck and Bubbles, and recites his song Bubbles.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: theater in the City of Los Angeles, every theater in the City of Frisco, in London, every theater in Scotland and Glasgow, Edinburgh and every theatre in San Francisco, every theater in Philadelphia, Atlantic City, every cabaret you could think of that's worthwhile. You name it. Just think that over a while. You can't name no theater or no cafe that Buck and Bubbles haven't played in. Now that's a whole lot. What big show have Buck and Bubbles not played in, from the little show to the big show, we've been in all of them. In fact we had a show of our own called Hot Chops and a fella, his name was -- what was his name -- aw, Lord, I can't think of the fella's name that wrote a song for Buck and I called Adison Carey. He wrote a song called Buck and Bubbles. I don't remember how the song goes now, but I wrote a song called "Bubbles." "Who am I to blame If Bubbles is the name It's not a mystery Bubbles may burst in the air Them bubbles may never get anywhere It isn't in a name that one should be ashamed. . ."
I can't think of the words to that song. That's the song I wrote for "Bubbles." Then I wrote another song called "Somebody's Going To Make You Fall in Love," that's another one.
The "Bubbles" song was on your album, wasn't it?
No. "I'm Forever Blowing Bubbles" on the album. Okay? Give me something else.
